lina: quick heads-up — ran a replay vs synthetic sweep on ded-32 yesterday and saw a ~45ms coldstart tail when kernel=fast_attn and kv miss ratio > 0.6. feels like a priming/regression interaction.

mike: ugh. can you paste the run config and the perf numbers?

lina: sure — run args: `./bench --mode=replay --pool=ded-32 --kernels=fast_attn,matmul --kv-policy=auto --burst=enabled --replay=trace_2026-03-16.json`

lina: summary csv: `qps,95p_ms,99p_ms,kv_miss_ratio` -> `1200,82,210,0.18` (synthetic) vs `1180,87,255,0.62` (replay). coldstart windows show 180–220ms spikes.

loadbot: automated note: replay run 1888312345 completed. artifacts at s3://redwood-perf/replays/1888312345/ (logs, profiles, flamegraphs).

chen: I pushed a kernel-selector tweak two days ago that biases matmul for short sequences when observed seq_mean < 128. Could be routing into fast_attn for sequences that still amplify KV misses.

mike: can you diff the selector?

chen: diff snippet: ```diff
- if (seq_mean < 128) choose=matmul;
+ if (seq_mean < 128 && kv_miss_pred < 0.4) choose=matmul;
```

sam: ok that explains it — the selector used historical seq_mean but not the per-window kv_miss_pred. replay traces have a phase where kv gets cold; selector kept routing to fast_attn which has worse cold KV priming behavior.

anita: flamegraph highlights: majority of extra 99p came from `kv_fetch` and `kv_lock_wait`. attaching two lines: `kv_fetch latency p99=140ms`, `kernel exec delta p99=45ms` — so KV is the dominant factor for tail.

lina: hypothesis: two compounding effects — (A) kernel that optimizes compute but assumes warmed KV (fast_attn) gets hammered when KV miss ratio high, (B) autoscaler scale-up path touches new GPUs with cold KV caches, and burst credits get consumed on other pools so we're not priming correctly.

mike: action items?

sam: propose short experiments (1) run replay with `--warmup-prefix=30s` to pre-prime KV, (2) run synthetic with an injected kv_miss_profile to mimic replay, (3) flip kernel-selector to check `kv_miss_pred` gating. each run should record: coldstart latency timeline, per-gpu kv hitrate, burst credit usage, and kernel selection percent.

lina: timeline: I'll run (1) today on ded-32 (low risk), sam can do (2) on a sandbox pool, chen will test selector change in branch and we can do A/B on a canary dedicated pool.

loadbot: enqueue job: `replay --trace trace_2026-03-16.json --warmup-prefix 30s --out s3://redwood-perf/1888312345/priming-exp/` -> job 2938

anita: small note — when investigating burst credits, remember dedicated pools have a different credit accrual model vs hosted. we saw clipped priming previously when credits were zeroed during rapid scale events. log snippet: `burst_credits: available=0 -> scale_event -> available=0` meaning no headroom to absorb priming spike.

mike: should we fallback policy to matmul when kv_miss_pred > 0.5 during scale-up windows? seems safer for tail.

chen: agree. I'll prototype a short-circuit: if (scale_up_in_progress && kv_miss_pred > 0.5) choose=matmul. keeps latency stable while we warm kv.

lina: good. also capture an apples-to-apples: run canary with identical sequences across both selector versions and toggle burst credits off/on to isolate credit effects.

sam: one trick — measure scale-up time in two phases: (A) infra spin (GPU ready), (B) KV warm (first kv hit percentile). scale-up SLA should be measured as A+B. right now A is ~12s and B can be 30–90s depending on workload.

anita: agreed. we should also add kv-priming hooks in the runtime to pre-populate local caches during GPU init when trace-based warmup is available. that would reduce B significantly.

lina: ok I'll file a short RFC for the runtime priming hook, and we'll run the experiments. posting results back here. thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: thanks — ping if you need me to run the A/B on prod-canary.

loadbot: job 2938 started (approx ETA 25m). artifacts will appear under s3://redwood-perf/1888312345/priming-exp/

lina: logging note — please annotate runs with `kernel_selector_experiment=true` and `kv_warmup=30s` tags so Optimize can attribute cost/quality changes.

sam: copied. will also add a small eval harness to check token-level quality drift when switching kernels during scale-up.

anita: last thought — we should collect a small sample of 'cold' inference traces (first N requests after scale) and run them through profiler offline to make targeted KV prefetch heuristics (not just full trace replay).

lina: perfect. closing loop after loadbot artifacts are in.
